input.question: why do our fingers randomly tingle sometimes?
input.ground_truth: That sounds like a possible nerve condition, and is not normal. Now I don't know if this is so serious that you need to run to the emergency room, but you might bring it up the next time you see your doctor. I know I had a friend in school who had a nerve condition, and it caused his fingers, and his toes to tingle periodically. The only times I feel a tingling in my extremes, is when I've sat, or laid wrong, and put a limb to sleep. Otherwise, if it's happening, seemingly spontaneously, then you may have some cause for concern.

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine your fingers are like little toys that have tiny wires inside them. Sometimes, those wires get a little mixed up or get a funny feeling, kind of like when your toy gets a little stuck and starts to wiggle or buzz. That funny feeling is called "tingling." It happens because your brain is sending little messages to your fingers, but sometimes the messages get a bit mixed up or take a funny path. It doesn’t hurt, it just feels weird! It can happen when you sit in one position too long, or when your hand "falls asleep." Then, when you move your hand or shake it, the messages start working right again, and the tingling goes away.
